findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

The approach is mostly coherent. It opens with a clear mental model, puts the riskiest assumption (assertion mapping) first, isolates execution in a detached clone, stores attempts in an append-only authenticated store and keeps observation separate from completion authority. Data, measurement, persona, surface and architecture-record coverage are present, and the durable ARCHITECTURE.md link resolves. Focused reviewability: pass. The decisions stay on the main review path, though some rows of the data table and the evidence-record boilerplate could be cut. Three blocking gaps remain. (1) Verification currency does not decide how changed toolchain, runtime and installed-dependency inputs affect current success. (2) Rollout is not decided. (3) The content of the required-assertion mapping, and who reviews it, is handed to Execution Planning, whose approval explicitly does not cover design. There are also non-blocking warnings: scenario counts and rows that don't match the bound feature file, principle proofs that can't establish their claims, and license fields in the evidence records that contradict the plan's own text.

Verification currency does not cover execution inputs outside the tracked tree. R4 says verification compares execution inputs with current inputs and refuses current success when they change, and dimensions.md requires observer-freshness to cover toolchain and profile changes. But 'CLI and currency' defines the currency projection as the tracked product tree plus ticket fields. Toolchain is only recorded at execution time, and its effect on verification is never stated. 'Schema/profile/runtime incompatibility refuses' covers only incompatibility, not a changed tool version or digest. The installed dependency tree existed only in the deleted clone, and Verify has no network or mutation, so it cannot be recomputed. Consequence: one valid implementation reports an observation as current after a Node, Bun, Git or Vitest version change, or after a dependency-host change that leaves the lockfile alone. That is a false current-success claim under R4. Owner: Implementation Planning. Fix: decide which recorded execution identities verification recomputes (tool paths, versions and digests; observer runtime and profile; lockfile and manifests as the stand-in for the dependency tree, with its confidence limit stated) and the refusal for each. Add the matching freshness proof row.

Rollout is not decided. The required content for this phase includes rollout and rollback, and the rubric requires rollout to be decided or explicitly not applicable. The plan has rollback only (in the Data table). It does not say how the new public commands and the bundled T3E4NS profile ship. In particular, it does not say whether the leaves exist only in the npm CLI or also in the generated Claude and Codex plugin bundles, which embed their own CLI and templates. Spec Reversibility says the public purpose and verification meaning are one-way. Consequence: the exposure boundary, and which installed runtime counts as the trusted profile source, are left to the implementer. Owner: Implementation Planning. Fix: add a rollout decision covering distribution channels, exposure (on by default or not) and how the observer/verifier runtime version is chosen, or give an explicit not-applicable reason for each.

The content of the required-assertion mapping, and who reviews it, is deferred to Execution Planning. R1 requires the fixed scope and mapping to come from the observer's 'reviewed, shipped contract'. The plan names mapping feasibility as its riskiest assumption, then says 'Execution Planning must enumerate the explicit expanded tuples ... and its review must inspect the mapping'. It also says later profile changes need a 'reviewed new shipped contract' without naming the review. Execution Planning approval covers startable delivery, not design. The case-to-assertion tuples, including which single assertion may support several cases, are the decision-bearing data contract for success. Consequence: no accepted owner ever approves the mapping that decides when success is issued, and the riskiest assumption reaches implementation unresolved. Owner: Implementation Planning (contract authority), with the user deciding any review route that widens scope. Viable choices: (a) attach the enumerated mapping as subordinate evidence linked from impl-plan.md and review it now; (b) keep enumeration later but name a dedicated contract-review authority and its approval meaning, from the existing review kinds or a user-accepted addition, and state that implementation cannot rely on the mapping until that review passes. To resume: record either choice in impl-plan.md and request fresh review.

The plan's scenario counts and rows don't match the bound feature file. The plan says the observer has '12 blocks / 17 compiled examples'. The bound feature file compiles to 14 cases (12 blocks; the outline has 3 rows). It also has no 'Candidate advances during the run' scenario and no paired semantic-versus-bookkeeping outline; it has two separate R4 scenarios, which the plan merges into one row. Every bound scenario is still covered. Before approval, confirm whether the packet's feature file or the plan's 'Available proof' claim is current, and correct the stale one.

Several Design alignment proofs can't establish their consequence. Principle 6 ('reuse durable writes ... no database, new dependency') cites impl-plan.md itself as proof, which is self-referential and can't discriminate. The NTB principle cites the feature file, but the stated consequence (a maintainer walkthrough) isn't checked by any scenario. Fix: name proof that could actually fail, such as a dependency-manifest diff or contract check and the planned walkthrough record.

The PlanEvidenceRecordV1 entries mark every license, security and reuse limit as 'none_declared'. But the plan says installed Vitest declares MIT, and its Implementation Inspiration table states real security limits ('documentation is not sandbox protection', 'same-user signing authority remains trusted'). Fill the records from the actual repository licenses and the limits the plan already states, so the machine-readable evidence matches the prose.

Strengths: the mid-run HEAD check is strict even for bookkeeping-only commits. Required-result proof is discriminated at the subprocess-output boundary. The retry-preservation proof starts from a nonempty diagnostic. Data ownership agrees with source-of-truth authority. The durable architecture record is linked and its status is honestly labeled proposed.
